options.text: The ionic bonds are very weak and break easily
The ions are too far apart to hold the structure together
When layers shift, like charges end up next to each other and repel, causing the crystal to shatter
The delocalised electrons cannot hold the layers in place

questions.explanation: When a force is applied to an ionic compound, layers of ions can shift. This causes ions with the same charge to be next to each other. The repulsion between like charges causes the crystal to shatter, making ionic compounds brittle.
